page.layout: One page of text in one column, a Hebrew dictionary entry page. Running head centred at the top, page number top right. Entries are paragraphs opened by a large Hebrew headword, with Latin glosses and Scripture references. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: plura observata sunt, ut Jef.49.5. & 1.Par.11.20. Job.6.21. Item bis scriptū לו, quod legendum לא Non, 1.Sam.2.16. & 20.2. הלא Nonne, Annon? Jos.10.13. vel cum Van, הלוא 1.Reg.1.11. Et cum He, הלה Nonne, Deut.3.11. בלוא In non, In id quod non, Jer.2.11. Pro non, i.e. Sine, Absq;, Jes.55.1. Per non, per eos qui non, Jer.5.7. כלוא Ac si non, Obad.16. ללוא In qui non, Jes.63.1. Absque, 2.Par.15.3. Chald. לא Non, Jerem.10.11. הלא Nonne, Dan.3.24. Et cum He; כלה Ut nihili, Dan.4.32.
לאב תלאונה f. Siccitas: Plurale, בארץ תלאבות [?] In terra siccitatum, id est, ficca, Hos.13.5.

לאה Molestè, Ægrè ferre: Laborare, Labore defetisci, Defatigari, Defessum esse. Futurum, תלאה Ægrè feres, Job.4.2. Cum apocopa, תלא Defetisceris, Job.4.5. וילאו Et defessi sunt, Genes.19.11. Niph.Præterit. נלאו Fatigatus fuit, Jes.16.12. נלאתי Defessus sum, Jer.1.14. Hiph. הלאה Fatigavit: Præter. הלאני Fatigat me, Job.16.7. הלאת Fatigat, Ezech.24.12. ubi ת est loco ה. Futur. תלאו Fatigatis, Jes.7.13.
תלאה f. Labor, Defatigatio, Molestia, Exod.18.8. מתלאה Quantum fatigationis, Malach.1.13. pro מה־תלאה sicut alibi dicitur מה זה pro מה־זה Exod.4.2.
לאט Obvolvit, Involvit, Involucris texit: Præter. לאט את־פניו Obvolvit faciem suam, 2.Sam.19.4. Vide & Job.15.11. Affine est verbo לוט.

לאך מלאך Legatus, Nuncius: Angelus: qui sic dicitur à Functione, quam Deus ipsi imponit, à מלאכה Functio. Constr. מלאך יהוה Angelus Domini, Gen.16.17. Aff. מלאכו Angelum suum, Gen.24.40. Plur. מלאכים Nuncios, Genes.32.3. Construct. מלאכי Angeli Dei,

page.notes: Hebrew words printed without full vowel pointing; consonants copied as seen, with [?] where letters are doubtful (notably the headword and the forms after "Vide infra in" and in the first entry). Large headwords (לאב, לאה, לאט, לאך) are printed in larger type and are treated as paragraph openings, not headings. The last line ends with a comma as printed; the entry continues on the next page.
